main_text.l: QUOMODO, DICET ALIQUIS, hæc omnia ad usum meum transferre potero.
Si sæpius & religiosè tecum ipse perpē-deris, circumstantias & causas tuæ couer-sionis & illuminationis, & auctori tantæ benedictionis summas egeris gratias.

Primū enim cogitandum, quà tua ætate, & apud quos versanti, concessa sit vberior cognitio mysteriorum Christi, ut è quib. ignorantiæ tenebris in admirabilé lucé sis edu-ctus, quibus in locis sis versatus, grato animo tandem agnoscas. Alij serius, alij citius illustrantur à spiritu sancto: qui omnia suo tempore agit: & ij, qui ab errore in viam ve-ritatis reducuntur (multum difsimiles ijs, qui sibi nihil discendum: & in semel concepta opinione perseuerandum putant.) alijs in locis alia experiuntur & discunt, quia in omnes proficiendi occasiones sunt intenti: & Deo aures eorum perforante, dociles, & veritatis studiosi redduntur.

Secundò & illud spectandum, quorum mi-nisterio & fideli institutione interuenie-te, in vera doctrina profeceris. Test̃ Lucas in Actis Apostolicis, Apollo, Alexandrinus, elo-quenté virū & in Scripturis potentē, initiatū in via domini, ab Aquila & Priscilla afsu-tū[?].

page.notes: Page number "131" at top right is hard to read; marked [?]. Running head "COMMENTARIA" is clear. "afsu-tū" at the end of the last line is partly cut off at the line end and the word is uncertain. "interuenie-te" and "elo-quenté" are uncertain in their final letters. "Test̃" uses a tilde over t, as printed. Printed "benedictionis" and "lucé" may carry accents I could not confirm. Printed "quib." with its stop is kept. The "&" under the text at right is not a catchword and is left out.
